question: At what coolant temperature does the L/R ENG TEMP warning illuminate?
explanation: AFM 3.2.2: L/R ENG TEMP indicates coolant temperature in the upper red range, above the 105 °C limit.

question: If L/R ENG TEMP illuminates during climb and no L/R COOL LVL caution is displayed, what is the first response?

options.text: Open ALTERNATE AIR and continue the climb unchanged
Reduce power on the affected engine by 10% or more and increase airspeed by 10 KIAS or more
Immediately shut down and feather the affected engine
Switch the VOTER to the opposite ECU

explanation: AFM 3.2.2: with no coolant-level caution shown, the first step during climb is to reduce power on the affected engine by at least 10% and increase airspeed by at least 10 KIAS.

question: If the L/R COOL LVL caution IS displayed together with L/R ENG TEMP, what should the pilot expect?

options.text: No further action is needed since the fault is only cosmetic
The affected engine should be run at maximum power to purge the coolant
A further increase in coolant temperature, and should prepare for an engine failure
The temperature will self-correct within 60 seconds

explanation: AFM 3.2.2: when L/R COOL LVL is also displayed, expect loss of coolant and a further temperature rise; prepare for an engine failure per 3.7.6.

question: At what oil temperature does the L/R OIL TEMP warning illuminate?
explanation: AFM 3.2.3: L/R OIL TEMP indicates oil temperature in the upper red range, above 140 °C.

question: If L/R OIL TEMP illuminates and oil pressure is outside the green range (low), what should be expected?

options.text: Loss of engine oil, and a further temperature increase — prepare for an engine failure
A faulty oil temperature sensor, since pressure should rise with temperature
Nothing unusual — this is a normal combination in cold weather
An imminent gearbox failure rather than an engine oil problem

explanation: AFM 3.2.3: if oil pressure is also outside the green range when L/R OIL TEMP illuminates, expect loss of engine oil and prepare for an engine failure per 3.7.6.

question: At what oil pressure does the L/R OIL PRES warning illuminate?
explanation: AFM 3.2.4: L/R OIL PRES indicates oil pressure in the lower red range, below 0.9 bar, which can lead to a total loss of power.

question: What is the immediate action for L/R FUEL PRESS if fuel quantity and the fuel selector are already checked and the pump is ON but the warning remains?

options.text: Switch the ALTERNATOR of the affected engine OFF
Open ALTERNATE AIR on both engines
Set the FUEL SELECTOR of the affected engine to CROSSFEED

explanation: AFM 3.2.7: after checking fuel quantity, selector and pump, if the warning persists the next step is CROSSFEED on the affected engine's fuel selector; if it still remains, expect an imminent engine failure.

question: At what alternator output does the L/R ALTN AMPS warning illuminate?
explanation: AFM 3.2.8: L/R ALTN AMPS is a warning-level annunciation for alternator output above the 70 A limit; the crew is directed to 3.10.2 - HIGH CURRENT.

question: If BOTH alternators fail at the same time, how long should battery power be expected to last?
explanation: AFM 3.3.1 warns that with both alternators failed, battery power should last about 30 minutes, after which engine stoppage should be expected.

question: Following a total loss of the Air Data Computer (ADC), what should the pilot use?

options.text: The emergency compass and standby attitude module only
The standby airspeed indicator and altimeter
The G1000 MFD engine page exclusively

explanation: AFM 3.5.4: ADC failure is shown by a red X and yellow text over airspeed, altimeter, vertical speed, TAS and OAT; the pilot must revert to the standby airspeed indicator and altimeter.

question: Following a total AHRS failure, what should the pilot revert to?

options.text: The magnetic compass and turn coordinator on the PFD
There is no backup; the flight must land immediately at the nearest airfield

explanation: AFM 3.4.2: an ATTITUDE FAIL annunciation removes the sky/ground presentation; the pilot must revert to the standby attitude indicator.

question: If both ECU A and ECU B cautions appear simultaneously with a perceived thrust reduction, what should the power lever be moved to first?

options.text: MAX immediately, to restore full thrust
IDLE and left there until landing
50% load and held there for 5 minutes
IDLE for 1 second, then slowly increased

explanation: AFM 3.7.2 (Engine Troubleshooting) directs the power lever to IDLE for 1 second, then a slow increase — not exceeding 1975 RPM — to identify and work around the power loss.

question: During engine troubleshooting, what maximum propeller speed should not be exceeded when slowly increasing power after a power loss?
explanation: AFM 3.7.2 warns not to increase the power lever past 1975 RPM (or the speed at which power loss was previously observed), as this leads into another power loss.

question: At what maximum reduced propeller speed can the affected engine still provide up to 65% power during the troubleshooting procedure?
explanation: A note in AFM 3.7.2 states that with this reduced power setting the engine can still provide up to 65% power at the maximum propeller speed of 1975 RPM.

question: If a landing gear unsafe light remains illuminated for longer than how many seconds during retraction or extension, should the gear selector be recycled?
explanation: AFM 3.9.1: if the unsafe light stays on beyond 20 seconds, check airspeed below vLOR (152 KIAS) and re-cycle the gear selector.

question: Up to what airspeed can the landing gear be extended manually?
explanation: AFM 3.9.2: the landing gear can be extended manually up to 152 KIAS, and the manual extension may take up to 20 seconds.

question: In cold ambient temperatures, if landing gear indicator lights do not confirm down-and-locked after manual extension, what airspeed should be used while applying moderate yaw and pitch inputs?
explanation: AFM 3.9.1/3.9.2 recommend reducing airspeed below 110 KIAS and applying moderate yawing and pitching to help the gear lock in cold conditions.

question: After a complete failure of the electrical system, for how long will the ECU backup batteries provide electrical power solely to the ECUs?
explanation: AFM 3.10.1 states the ECU backup batteries provide electrical power to the ECUs for at least 30 minutes after a complete electrical failure.

question: After a complete electrical failure, for how long will the backup artificial horizon and flood light have electrical power?
explanation: AFM 3.10.1 states the backup artificial horizon (or standby attitude module) and the flood light have power for at least 1.5 hours, since they run from the separate emergency battery.

question: Where is the cabin hand fire extinguisher located?

options.text: On the RH side of the cabin floor, behind the co-pilot seat

explanation: AFM 3.11 states the cabin hand fire extinguisher is located inside the passenger compartment on the RH side of the cabin floor behind the co-pilot seat.

question: What is the maximum demonstrated airspeed for emergency opening of the front canopy in flight (e.g. for smoke evacuation)?
explanation: AFM 3.11.5/3.12.1 state the maximum demonstrated airspeed for opening the front canopy in the cooling-gap position in flight is 117 KIAS.

question: After an ELECTRICAL FIRE IN FLIGHT checklist switches the ELECT. MASTER off, what system still provides power to the standby attitude gyro and flood light?

options.text: The emergency battery, once the EMERGENCY switch is set ON
The RH alternator, which stays connected independently
The main 24V battery, which is never disconnected

explanation: AFM 3.11.5 explains that switching the EMERGENCY switch ON lets the separate emergency battery supply the standby attitude gyro/module and flood light even after ELECT. MASTER is OFF.

question: Below what airspeed should the airplane be flown if the canopy or rear passenger door is found unlocked in flight?
explanation: AFM 3.12.2 requires reducing airspeed below 140 KIAS for either an unlocked canopy or an unlocked rear passenger door before landing at the next suitable airfield.

question: What is the correct response if the rear passenger door comes open in flight and separates from the airplane?

options.text: Attempt an immediate off-airport landing regardless of terrain
Deploy the emergency axe to widen the opening for evacuation
Reduce to stall speed to minimize aerodynamic loads
Continue flight — the airplane can be safely flown to the next suitable airfield

explanation: A note under AFM 3.12.2 states that if the door has been lost, the airplane can be safely flown to the next suitable airfield; but the crew must never attempt to re-lock the door in flight.

question: What hazard is specifically associated with a front baggage door coming open in flight?

options.text: Separation of the door may damage the propeller and could lead to an engine failure
Loss of static pressure reference for the ADC
Immediate loss of electrical power to the RH bus

explanation: AFM 3.12.2 warns that separation of the front baggage door may damage the propeller and lead to an engine failure.

question: If the propeller RPM oscillates and the problem does not clear with a power setting change, what should be checked next?

options.text: The G1000 for an L/R ECU A/B FAIL caution, then move the VOTER switch to the other ECU
The fuel selector, and immediately move it to CROSSFEED
The landing gear position indicator lights

explanation: AFM 3.12.3(a): for oscillating RPM, if changing the power setting does not help, check for an ECU A/B FAIL caution and switch the VOTER to the unaffected ECU.

question: If unintentional flight into icing occurs, what should be done with the POWER lever?

options.text: Keep it fixed at the current setting to avoid shock-cooling
Set it to exactly 92% and leave it there for the remainder of the flight
Increase power, applying periodic power changes to prevent ice build-up on the propeller blades
Reduce to idle to minimize propeller loading

explanation: AFM 3.12.4 directs increasing power and applying periodic power changes to prevent ice accumulation on the propeller blades while leaving the icing area.

question: What is the very first (and most fundamental) response taught for recovering from an unintentional spin?

options.text: Full aft elevator to reduce airspeed
Full power on the outside engine to accelerate rotation stop
Ailerons fully into the spin direction
Power lever IDLE, full rudder against the spin, elevator fully forward, and ailerons neutral — carried out simultaneously

explanation: AFM 3.12.6 requires steps 1-4 (power IDLE, opposite rudder, elevator fully forward, ailerons neutral) to be carried out immediately and simultaneously; single-engine stalling is not permitted at all.

question: During the emergency descent procedure, what should the airspeed never exceed?

options.text: vLE = 188 KIAS only with gear down

explanation: AFM 3.12.7 warns not to exceed vNE (188 KIAS) during an emergency descent, flown with flaps UP, gear DOWN and power at IDLE.

question: What position is selected for the landing gear during an emergency descent, and why?

options.text: Manual extension only, since the electrical gear pump is inhibited above vNO
DOWN, to increase drag and steepen the descent
UP, to minimize drag and maximize the descent rate
As required by airspeed only, gear position is irrelevant

explanation: AFM 3.12.7 selects gear DOWN (with flaps UP and power IDLE) specifically to increase drag for a rapid emergency descent.

question: What must be done SIMULTANEOUSLY when disengaging the autopilot after an autopilot or electric trim malfunction?

options.text: Switch the AVIONIC MASTER off before grasping the controls
Release the CWS switch before grasping the control stick
Grasp the control stick firmly to regain control while depressing and holding the AP DISC switch
Pull the AUTOPILOT circuit breaker before touching the control stick

explanation: AFM 3.12.9 requires items 1 and 2 — grasping the stick and pressing AP DISC — to be accomplished simultaneously, followed by retrimming and pulling the AUTOPILOT circuit breaker.

question: After an autopilot malfunction is corrected, when may the autopilot be re-engaged?

options.text: Immediately, once the AP DISC switch is released
After a single circuit-breaker reset, regardless of cause
After 5 minutes have elapsed, regardless of cause
Only after the cause of the malfunction has been corrected

explanation: AFM 3.12.9 warns not to attempt to re-engage the autopilot or manual electric trim until the cause of the malfunction has been corrected.
